layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-02.1 Vulnerability Identification
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective:
Vulnerabilities — including, where in scope,
AI-system-specific attack surfaces (data poisoning, model poisoning,
adversarial examples, model evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws)
— are identified on a continuing basis across the system, product, ICT
asset, or AI system that an entity operates, manufactures, deploys, or
processes, with the resulting identification artefact (vulnerability
register, risk-scenario catalogue, SBOM, or risk-management file) feeding
the entity's testing, remediation, and notification cascades.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y for the dual-scope entity; **NOT scope-disjoint** for the personal-data-breach sub-event at a NSIE.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge on the identification pipeline; layered cascade on the disclosure pathway. The identification layer (vulnerability discovery + validation + recording) is unified; the disclosure layer branches to SA (GDPR) and CSIRT (NIS 2) with the divergence lives in D-04.3 timeline analyses.

pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge with advisory ingestion. The CRA product's SBOM and vulnerability-advisory pipeline feeds the controller's Art. 32(1)(d) testing register.

pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge with DORA-cadenced floor. The DORA testing programme (continuous + at-least-yearly scenario review) discharges both obligations.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y for the controller deploying high-risk AI processing personal data.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Layered stack with AI-specific overlay. The GDPR conventional testing covers the conventional threat model; the AI Act Art. 9 + 15(4)–(5) adds the AI-specific attack taxonomy.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y on the single dual-scope entity; the manufacturer-vs-entity actor split can be disjoint in baseline.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge with institutional pathway. The CRA product-side identification feeds the NIS 2 entity-side CVD architecture.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y for the dual-scope entity; N/A (lex specialis) for pure-financial.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** DORA-cadenced floor absorbs NIS 2 for financial entities; cross-sector entities stack-merge.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y on the dual-scope entity.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Layered stack with AI-specific overlay.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y on the dual-scope deployment; disjoint in baseline (manufacturer ≠ financial entity).
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge with SBOM ingestion. The CRA SBOM is an upstream input to the DORA asset-vulnerability register via supplier-correspondence.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y on integrated edge-AI products; disjoint in baseline.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Stack-merge with deemed-compliance bridge. CRA-Compliant product + AI Act Art. 9 + 15(4)–(5) AI-specific layer.

pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Y on the dual-scope deployment.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Layered stack with AI-specific overlay. DORA's continuous ICT risk identification + AI Act's AI-specific risk identification cycle + Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-specific attack taxonomy.

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.1 Data Minimisation
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Data collected or otherwise acquired is limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the purpose for which it is processed, with a documented necessity assessment and, where the underlying purpose changes, a compatibility assessment confirming that the new use is consistent with the original. Special-category data is processed only where a narrow exception applies and is documented to that effect.
layer0_subdomain_refs.objective: Data collected or otherwise acquired is limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the purpose for which it is processed, with a documented necessity assessment and, where the underlying purpose changes, a compatibility assessment confirming that the new use is consistent with the original. Special-category data is processed only where a narrow exception applies and is documented to that effect.

pairs.scope_overlap: Conditional (Y when the same dataset contains personal data and is processed by a CRA-classified product at runtime)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Conditional (Y when the same personal-data stream flows through a CRA-classified product at runtime)**. The two obligations stack rather than contradict.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a 2-track minimisation matrix: (1) GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) + Art. 6(4) personal-data minimisation with compatibility assessment; (2) CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) product-data minimisation. For CRA-regulated products processing personal data, the union applies. The Art. 6(4) compatibility test is GDPR-only and must be retained as a residual obligation.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y when training a high-risk AI system with bias-detection needs that cannot be met by other data.
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y only for the narrow Art. 10(5) carve-out scenario: a high-risk AI provider training a system with bias-detection needs that cannot be met by non-special-category data.** Outside that narrow window, the AI Act does not trigger special-category processing, so the pair does not overlap. The pair is therefore scope-disjoint in baseline, with the carve-out as the single overlap point.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must codify AI Act Art. 10(5) as a **gateway clause** that *expands* the set of permissible special-category processing under GDPR Art. 9(1) when all 6 conditions are satisfied. The CRDA "contradictory" label should be corrected to "scope-disjoint" with carve-out annotation. Phase 3 case generation must surface the 6-condition matrix explicitly when the case company is a high-risk AI provider processing special-category data for bias correction.

pairs.scope_overlap: N (typically)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **N (typically)**. They are layered at different lifecycle stages. The only overlap is at the data-flow boundary (training data → runtime data) which is sequential, not concurrent.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a 3-track minimisation matrix for AI-enabled CRA products (runtime minimisation + personal-data minimisation + training-data quality). Phase 3 case generation must validate that the runtime product does not retain more data than the training-data quality permits to flow into it.

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.2 Retention & Archiving
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Data — across the data classes in scope — is retained for the period required to satisfy its declared purpose, with documented retention rationale and, where the underlying purpose changes, a reset of the retention clock. Long-term archiving or research-only retention is paired with safeguards proportional to the residual identifiability.
layer0_subdomain_refs.objective: Data — across the data classes in scope — is retained for the period required to satisfy its declared purpose, with documented retention rationale and, where the underlying purpose changes, a reset of the retention clock. Long-term archiving or research-only retention is paired with safeguards proportional to the residual identifiability.

pairs.scope_overlap: N (typically)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Conditional (Y when a CRA update-distribution log contains personal data, the controller must apply GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) to the personal data portion; CRA Annex I Part II (7)/(8) applies to the artefact portion independently).** In the typical case (pure update artefacts with no personal data), there is no overlap. The pair is therefore scope-disjoint in baseline.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must correct CRDA's "contradictory" label to "scope-disjoint" with separation-architecture requirement. The 3-axis retention policy (GDPR ceiling + CRA availability + AI Act floor) is correct as a *layering* rule, but the CRDA label "contradictory" is scope-incorrect. Phase 3 case generation must validate that CRA-regulated products with personal-data-containing update logs apply separation architecture (pseudonymisation, separate retention rules) to honour both

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when AI-system logs contain personal data)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when AI-system logs contain personal data, both GDPR and AI Act apply on the same log set at the same controller / provider)**. The two obligations are reconcilable within the intersection [6 months, "necessary"]. The pair is substantive-complementary, not scope-disjoint.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must codify AI Act Art. 19(1) as a *floor* within the GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) *ceiling* envelope. The CRDA "contradictory" label should be corrected to "complementary". Phase 3 case generation must validate that high-risk AI providers set the AI Act 6-month floor as a hard minimum and the GDPR "necessary" boundary as the cap.

pairs.scope_overlap: N
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **N** — distinct actors, distinct objects, distinct triggers.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation is straightforward: two parallel obligations. No layering required; both apply simultaneously when the same actor is both manufacturer (CRA) and provider (AI Act).

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-07.1 Secure-by-Design Principles
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Security is integrated into the acquisition, design, development, production, deployment and maintenance of systems and products via documented by-design decisions, risk-assessment propagation, proportionate safeguards, and lifecycle consistency.
layer0_subdomain_refs.objective: Security is integrated into the acquisition, design, development, production, deployment and maintenance of systems and products via documented by-design decisions, risk-assessment propagation, proportionate safeguards, and lifecycle consistency.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when the same entity is both a controller and an NSIE processing personal data through NIS).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the controller-NSIE designs NIS that processes personal data).** No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a joint by-design stack: GDPR Art. 25(1) outputs (data-protection properties) become inputs to the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) lifecycle evidence trail.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when the controller deploys a CRA-regulated product that processes personal data, OR when the manufacturer is also a controller for its own product telemetry).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the controller deploys a CRA-regulated product processing personal data)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a 2-track by-design matrix: (1) GDPR Art. 25(1) controller-side personal-data by-design; (2) CRA Art. 13(1)/(2) manufacturer-side product by-design with Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record.

pairs.scope_overlap: Conditional (Y when a financial entity is a controller processing personal data over its own ICT systems).

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when a high-risk AI system processes personal data and the provider/deployer is a controller).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the provider-deployer is a controller processing personal data via a high-risk AI system)**. No reclassification required.

Recital 78 preservation is the operative OJ cross-link.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when the entity procures a CRA-regulated product — they meet at the supplier-customer boundary).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the entity procures a CRA-regulated product and integrates it into NIS)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a supplier-customer interface map: CRA-conformant product serves as upstream gate for NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) deployment decisions; NIS 2 entity's supplier-risk register references CRA Annex VII technical documentation.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when a DORA financial entity is also an NSIE — both apply).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when a DORA financial entity is also an NSIE applying maintenance-phase controls)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a DORA-dominant stack: DORA Art. 9(4)(e) six-step process discharges both DORA's dedicated change-management obligation and NIS 2's maintenance-phase security requirement.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when NIS embeds a high-risk AI system).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when NIS embeds high-risk AI)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a layered AI-NIS stack: NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) lifecycle evidence + AI Act QMS design verification as separate artefacts.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when a DORA entity procures CRA-regulated products).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the DORA entity is also a CRA product deployer/procurer)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a CRA-as-upstream-gate model: CRA-conformant products are inputs to DORA's Art. 6(1) ICT risk-management framework.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (for AI-enabled CRA products, the same product is both CRA-regulated and AI-Act high-risk).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the same product is both CRA-regulated and AI-Act high-risk)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must operationalise CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2: a unified risk assessment under AI Act Art. 9 substitutes for CRA risk assessment when both apply. QMS (AI Act) + Annex I conformity (CRA) stack with documented cross-walk.

pairs.scope_overlap: Y (when a DORA financial entity deploys high-risk AI).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Y (when the DORA financial entity deploys high-risk AI)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a layered stack: DORA Art. 9(4)(e) change-management gate + AI Act QMS design-control governance.

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-07.2 Secure Coding Practices
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Coding practices deliver attack-surface limitation, exploitation mitigation, and AI-system attack-defence under an appropriate coding-practice evidence base.
layer0_subdomain_refs.objective: Coding practices deliver attack-surface limitation, exploitation mitigation, and AI-system attack-defence under an appropriate coding-practice evidence base.

pairs.scope_overlap: N (typically)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **N (typically)** — different objects (product coding outcomes vs. entity change process), different actors (manufacturer vs. financial entity). Pair is scope-disjoint in the OJ-literal reading; CRDA's "complementary" label is more a taxonomy artifact than a substantive relationship.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 1 entities must NOT treat DORA as a coding-standards authority absent OJ-text evidence (see P0 disagreement). Coding-standards baseline must be built from industry frameworks (NIST SSDF, OWASP SAMM, ISO 27034) and demonstrated against each regulation's outcome (CRA) or process (DORA) requirement.

pairs.scope_overlap: Conditional (Y when the CRA-regulated product is an AI-enabled product with high-risk AI components).
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **Conditional (Y for AI-enabled high-risk products; N for CRA-regulated products without AI)**. No reclassification required.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a layered coding-defence stack for AI-enabled CRA products: CRA Annex I (2)(j)/(k) generic coding + AI Act Art. 15(4)/(5) AI-specific attack-defence.

pairs.scope_overlap: N (typically)
pairs.scope_disjoint_test: ** Does this pair actually overlap on a single event at a single party? **N (typically)** — different objects, different actors, different lifecycle stages. Pair is substantively scope-disjoint; CRDA "complementary" is a taxonomy artifact.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce two parallel tracks: DORA change-management (Art. 9(4)(e)) + AI Act attack-defence (Art. 15(4)/(5)). No OJ-level consolidation rule exists for coding practices (unlike CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 AI-Act-substitution for risk assessment, which does not extend to coding).

tipo2.description: AI Act Art. 73 — high-risk AI providers have 3-tier reporting (initial notification, intermediate report, final report) to national authorities; Art. 73(2)-(4) specify content per tier.
tipo2.rationale: 3-tier reporting is structurally similar to DORA but different content requirements and recipients (national authority, not ESA).

tipo3.description: AI Act Art. 2(2) + Recital 19-21 — AI systems used exclusively for national security, defense, or military purposes are excluded from AI Act scope.
tipo3.rationale: National security carve-out. Companies doing dual-use AI may still be partially in scope for non-security components.
